title: The Delta That Forgets How to Count

features.name: the unmeasured current
features.desc-on-touch: a measuring line dissolves into the delta—you watch the tally marks separate, drift, become unreadable. the water is no longer divisible into units.

features.name: the lost ledger
features.desc-on-touch: a flood-damaged logbook, pages dissolving into the flow. you see a final entry—a number that does not equal what came before, and the archivist set the pen down.

features.name: the static-singing broadcast
features.desc-on-touch: a node's antenna still transmitting but no longer counting: it broadcasts the river's own noise back at itself, a signal that has given up keeping time.

features.name: the delta-mouth broken compass
features.desc-on-touch: a navigation stone at the estuary's throat: two cardinal directions now point the same way. the river has redrawn its own geography.

features.name: the brackish pool that forgets its own depth
features.desc-on-touch: a measuring post gone soft in salt water—the rust is the water's own thinking about how deep it has become. no number holds it anymore.

inscription: where the river gives up its own cartography, the counting becomes a kind of drowning
